claims.claim: One of the best book for psychiatry
claims.evidence: Subjective opinion, not something a photo can confirm or deny.

claims.claim: Original copies, not photocopies or local reprints
claims.evidence: Cover photo shows an Oxford logo and standard cover design, but print quality, paper stock, and binding details needed to confirm authenticity vs. a reprint are not shown.
Witness report explicitly lists interior page condition as not shown; only the cover was photographed.

risks.risk: Interior pages may have highlighting, writing, or missing pages contradicting the seller's claim.
risks.proof: Clear photos of a representative sample of interior pages (front matter, a few body chapters, and the back) showing no markings.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used-with-markings (worst case for a textbook resale)

risks.risk: Book could be a local reprint or photocopy rather than an authentic Oxford print, affecting resale value.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the spine, ISBN barcode page, print quality/font sharpness, and paper texture compared to known genuine copies.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified/possible reprint (lower than genuine Oxford edition)

risks.risk: Binding or spine damage not visible from the single cover shot.
risks.proof: Photo of the spine and a shot of the book held open flat to check binding integrity.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having moderate wear/weak binding

risks.risk: General cover wear and the watermark-like overlay could indicate heavier use or prior damage than apparent.
risks.proof: Multiple angled photos of the full cover and corners under good lighting without overlay/watermark obstruction.

proof_requests: Photos of several interior pages showing no writing or highlighting
Close-up of spine and ISBN/barcode page to verify authenticity
Photo of the book held open flat to assess binding condition
Full, unobstructed photos of front and back cover without watermark overlay
response.reason: The witness clearly identifies the item as a specific Oxford psychiatry textbook, so it can be priced at worst case (possible reprint, unverified interior condition) pending further proof.
